summary: Bound client usage reads to indexed cumulative snapshot boundaries

replay.detail: No claim or projection replay. Usage reads use the existing replicated rollups.

schema.detail: Adds the partial claims_usage_period_boundary_index on normalized series and observed timestamp expressions, and drops the obsolete claims_usage_rollup_index. Existing stores build the new index on first open; no table, schema-version or shared projection change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules, retention or digest change; canonical snapshot tie-breaking is preserved.

compatibility.detail: The client usage response and pairing scope are unchanged. Existing cumulative rollups remain readable, including missing attribution and pricing provenance.

downtime.detail: First open waits for SQLite to construct the partial index over existing claims. Index creation on an offline 1.79 GB store copy with 118390 claims and 3976 response rollups took 9.315 seconds on Linux x86_64 using SQLite 3.53.3. This is an index-only measurement, not daemon restart-to-API timing or the pinned Rust SQLite build; allow time for first-open construction. Later opens reuse the index.

manual.detail: No manual migration or client changes are required; index creation is automatic at store open.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back is supported: previous builds recreate their prior partial index, ignore the additional index, and retain the same claim data.
